history.dynasty: Phulkian (Patiala state) patronage; present building constructed under Maharaja Yadavindra Singh
history.period: Guru Tegh Bahadur's visit 24 January 1672 (Magh Sudi 5, 1728 Bikram); memorial garden under Raja Amar Singh of Patiala (1748-82); present building 1930-1942
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is the FAMOUS Sikh gurdwara Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib ('the eradicator of suffering') at Lehal, now part of Patiala city. Per local tradition recorded in an old handwritten document kept at the gurdwara, Bhag Ram, a jhivar of Lehal, asked the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, then staying at Saifabad (now Bahadurgarh), to visit and bless his village, which was afflicted by a serious and mysterious sickness. The Guru visited Lehal on Magh Sudi 5, 1728 Bikram (24 January 1672) and stayed under a banyan tree by the side of a pond; the sickness subsided, and the spot where the Guru sat came to be known as Dukh Nivaran. Devotees believe in the healing qualities of the sarovar's water. Raja Amar Singh of Patiala (1748-82) laid out a memorial garden on the site and entrusted it to Nihang Sikhs; an 1870 court case mentions a Guru's garden and a Nihangs' well here. In 1920, when a survey for the Sirhind-Patiala-Jakhal railway line threatened the sacred banyan tree, the men ordered to fell it refused, and Maharaja Bhupinder Singh cancelled the entire project. No gurdwara building stood until 1930, when a committee raised funds and began construction, completed twelve years later in 1942; Maharaja Yadavindra Singh built the present building and sarovar. It passed under Patiala state government administration, then the Dharam Arth Board of PEPSU, and finally the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC). CSV town Patiala is correct; district Patiala, Punjab. NOTE ON THE BRIEF: the task brief suggested a construction date of 1834 under Maharaja Karam Singh; no source found supports this — every consulted source (Wikipedia, holyshrines.in, sikh-heritage.co.uk) dates the present building to the 1930 fund-raising committee and 1942 completion under Maharaja Yadavindra Singh. Do not repeat the 1834/Karam Singh claim. SOURCE-CONFLATION FLAG: this is the authentic Patiala shrine whose documented history (Bhag Ram, 1672 visit, Raja Amar Singh's garden, 1942 building) many websites paste onto the separately listed Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib at Ludhiana — see 812.json, which documents that conflation and treats the Ludhiana gurdwara's own history as unverified.

name: Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib
town_description: Patiala, on Sirhind Road in southeastern Punjab, was the capital of the Phulkian princely state founded by Baba Ala Singh in 1763. The gurdwara stands at Lehal (now absorbed into the city, Factory Area / Upkar Nagar), one of Patiala's most-visited Sikh shrines alongside Qila Mubarak and the Kali Devi Temple.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, the nearest major airport (~65 km, verify); Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~155 km, verify).
travel.railway: Patiala Railway Station, less than 1 km away; autos and cycle rickshaws to the gurdwara.
travel.road: On Dukhniwaran Sahib Road / Sirhind–Patiala Road, Factory Area, Upkar Nagar; well connected by road within Patiala city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Gurpurabs for major congregations (crowded).
visitor_information.opening_hours: No fixed published hours found; gurdwaras are generally open from early morning to late evening daily — verify locally. Cover your head and remove shoes before entering; langar (free community meal) is served.
